-- w/scanlib/scan.lgo --
package scanlib

import (
	"comptime"
	"errors"
	"fmt"
)

func ScanField[F any](dst *F, path string) error {
	const switch F {
	case ~string:
		_ = &NotNullDest[F]{Dst: dst, Path: path}
		return nil
	}
	const if comptime.IsStruct[F]() {
		return errors.New("scanlib: struct in minimal probe")
	}
	return errors.New("scanlib: " + path + ": unsupported type")
}

type NotNullDest[V any] struct {
	Dst  *V
	Path string
}

// Convert exercises an unnamed case target: the shadow F binds *int, so
// F(p) must stay a conversion, not parse as a dereference of int(p).
func Convert[F any](p *int) int {
	const switch F {
	case *int:
		return *F(p)
	}
	return -1
}

// Embed exercises an alias to the case shadow in embedded position:
// struct{ G } keeps the field name G, so the keyed literal and selector
// must resolve.
func Embed[F any](v F) int {
	const switch F {
	case int:
		type G = F
		s := struct{ G }{G: 7}
		return s.G
	}
	return -1
}

// Capture exercises a case body that declares its own int: the shadow F
// must still mean the case's int, not the local string alias.
func Capture[F any](v F) int {
	const switch F {
	case int:
		type int = string
		var x F = v
		return x
	}
	return -1
}

func IntField[F any](v F) string {
	const switch F {
	case int:
		var x F = v
		_ = x
		return "int"
	}
	const if comptime.IsStruct[F]() {
		return "struct"
	}
	return "other"
}

// F shares a name with the parameters' shadows below: a nested call
// argument that resolves to F here instead of to the case's argument
// specializes for the wrong type.
type F = int

// Outer exercises a nested comptime call on a case shadow: Inner[F]
// must specialize for the case's argument even though a package type
// named F exists.
func Outer[F any](v F) string {
	const switch F {
	case ~string:
		return Inner[F](v)
	}
	return "other"
}

func Inner[T any](v T) string {
	const switch T {
	case ~string:
		return "str"
	}
	return "num"
}

// SameName exercises an argument spelled like the parameter: the case
// alias must bind F to the caller's F, never `type F = F`.
func SameName[F any](v F) string {
	const switch F {
	case ~string:
		return "same"
	}
	return "other"
}

// Both exercises another parameter's argument spelled like the case
// shadow: inside the case G is the caller's F, not the shadowed F.
func Both[F, G any](v G) string {
	const switch F {
	case int:
		return fmt.Sprintf("%T", v)
	}
	return "other"
}

-- w/main/main.lgo --
package main

import (
	"fmt"

	"example.com/copyshadow/scanlib"
)

type Status string

// F shares its name with the scanlib parameters' shadows.
type F string

func main() {
	var s Status
	if err := scanlib.ScanField[Status](&s, "s"); err != nil {
		panic(err)
	}
	fmt.Println("scan", scanlib.IntField[Status]("x"), scanlib.IntField[int](1))
	n := 4
	fmt.Println("copy", scanlib.Convert[*int](&n), scanlib.Embed[int](0), scanlib.Capture[int](3))
	fmt.Println("nest", scanlib.Outer[Status]("x"), scanlib.SameName[F]("y"), scanlib.Both[int, F](F("z")), scanlib.Outer[F]("x"))
}

-- w/scanlib/ext_test.lgo --
package scanlib_test

import (
	"testing"

	"example.com/copyshadow/scanlib"
)

type Status string

func TestDirectNamedCall(t *testing.T) {
	var s Status
	if err := scanlib.ScanField[Status](&s, "s"); err != nil {
		t.Fatalf("ScanField: %v", err)
	}
	if got := scanlib.IntField[Status]("x"); got != "other" {
		t.Fatalf("IntField[Status] = %q, want other", got)
	}
	if got := scanlib.IntField[int](1); got != "int" {
		t.Fatalf("IntField[int] = %q, want int", got)
	}
}
